preserved_behavior: Every particle/requested move/duplicate prior, original RNG and commit order, dictionary order and integer gauge are retained. No particle, candidate, search range or precision reduction.

MoveKeyMemoStep calls D228 staging/weight/choice code verbatim. Only staging canonical lookups use the local memo; actual bound methods, module globals, DD generation and native oracle remain unchanged.

Canonical first misses use the original function. Only plain builtin-integer dictionaries are reusable by retained identity; empty plain dictionaries return the original empty tuple. Unusual types bypass reuse. Frozen code does not mutate an H after its first memo lookup within that scope.

Full-epoch alternative binds unchanged method code objects to a private per-call state view and private globals. Only canonical lookup and same-problem canonical DD reuse are redirected. Original module globals and runtime methods are never temporarily patched.

Full-epoch memo retains hypothesis/problem identities, shares DD arrays only with frozen read-only consumers, and drops epoch references in finally on normal/skip/exception paths. Local staging memo ends before original per-particle commit copies.

All pinned-source/method guards, strict error-policy original complete-step fallback and unsupported native-score scalar fallback remain. Native FP64 formulas, original two IRLS iterations, thresholds and CUDA source/DLL are unchanged.
numerical_limits: All900 synthetic timed states and72 warm states match the prior same backend without numerical tolerance. GPU accuracy uses an untimed prior-GPU snapshot; do not compare GPU to CPU as an exact-bit requirement.
Four local-C++ prefixes across run1/run2/run3 and two seeds preserve all encoded state and trajectory array bits for1200 PF steps. Full-epoch C++ and local GPU each preserve200 same-backend steps.

D226/D227 native-vs-NumPy small arithmetic differences are unchanged. Reuse introduces no new tolerance. Prefix coverage does not complete full-route multi-seed positioning-error acceptance.
